availability taking time to check this information prevents misleading sprint capacity figures good habit start with members already in smn update existing records instead of creating duplicates 1 find the right team members 1 open team members and check the selected team 2 choose cards for browsing profiles or list to compare people 3 use name role function and status filters then select filter 4 review active and inactive groups someone who has left the team may still belong in its history 5 open a member record to review the details cards list is a local display preference it does not modify assignments 2 complete the profile why each field matters identity and professional function display name identifies the person in the roster and records email address optional contact information where relevant it does not determine team assignment professional function describes the person s job or specialty it is different from their agile role someone may divide their activity between development scrum master and product owner responsibilities location determines the national holiday calendar open location on the member record and review country two letter iso code identifies the member s country and the matching national public holidays region adds geographical context city identifies the usual working location time zone iana provides the member s time zone reference effective date indicates when the location version takes effect do you need to enter public holidays manually not for national holidays already included in smn s reference data the member calendar automatically looks up holidays for the country stored on that member s location record rather than using the installation country or another person s location example a team may include one person in france and another in india each calendar should show the national holidays of the corresponding country when those dates are included in smn s reference data always check the country not just the city or time zone important local or regional holidays are not guaranteed to be available check the calendar when a particular non working day matters for planning 3 define team assignment and agile roles open assignment assignment start and end dates determine when a person belongs to the team including for historical sprints understand the percentages contract percentage reference working time proportion allocation percentage the part assigned to the team the form checks that allocation does not exceed contract percentage contribution percentage describes the contribution configured for planning role distribution allocates 100 across scrum master product owner and developer as required by the form effective date records when a change becomes applicable preserving dated assignment versions example a part time employee may be assigned to the team for only part of their working time and split their responsibilities between development and scrum master duties their name alone cannot determine development capacity joining leaving and history 1 review the assignment start date 2 when a person leaves enter the end date and an optional reason 3 record changes of responsibility with a new dated version 4 correct a historical revision only to fix an earlier mistake ending an assignment is not the same as deleting the member 4 configure working days and half days open calendar then edit work calendar the form shows monday through sunday with two slots per day morning worked check when the member normally works in the morning afternoon worked check when the member normally works in the afternoon effective date defines when this weekly pattern starts to apply half day slots help represent a non working wednesday afternoon or a part time schedule when no schedule has been saved smn can suggest a monday to friday week with both half days worked a suggestion is not a validated schedule adjust and save it based on the person s real working pattern planning tip avoid copying one member s working week to everyone two developers with identical contract percentages may follow different schedules 5 check absences and calendar exceptions from the member record review the calendar and absences the absence form includes start and end dates half day slots a category a reason and whether the absence is planned or unplanned calendar exceptions capture one off changes to the normal working week national holidays available in smn are looked up automatically from the member s country so you do not need to create a manual absence for each supported holiday avoid duplicate absences and ensure dates fall within the relevant team assignment be careful with historical changes affecting closed sprints 6 how member information feeds team capacity team capacity is not simply headcount multiplied by sprint days several pieces of information matter together 1 assignment period is the member part of this team on the relevant dates 2 contract allocation and contribution how much activity should be considered 3 agile roles how is work distributed across development scrum master and product owner duties 4 personal work calendar which days and half days are worked 5 country and public holidays which national holidays apply to this member 6 absences and exceptions what changes the available working time these inputs inform availability worked day and capacity information in smn the exact calculation depends on the indicator s definition total person day capacity and development capacity need not include the same activities example a sprint covers ten usual working days one member only joins in week two another does not work wednesday afternoons and a third has a national holiday counting three people for ten full days would overstate availability 7 when capacity or holidays look wrong capacity too high check assignment end dates working patterns and missing absences capacity too low check assignment dates unchecked half days percentages and recorded absences missing public holiday verify the member s country code and that the holiday exists in smn s reference data wrong country s holiday correct the member s location not the global installation country unexpected historical result review dated versions and closed sprint states some closed sprint indicators may need to be refreshed by closing the sprint again after a correction your final check ask yourself are assignment dates correct do contract and role percentages reflect reality is the work schedule accurate does the country match the holiday calendar have absences been reviewed once these details are reliable your team is in a better position to plan sprints and interpret capacity indicators

articles.title: Sprint page: follow the complete life of a sprint
articles.searchText: sprint page follow the complete life of a sprint the sprint page is your team s working record it brings together goals ceremonies capacity indicators register items trends and the sprint review unlike the sprint list which helps you find and plan cycles this page helps you manage and understand one specific sprint camille s tip revisit the sprint page throughout the iteration not just at closure good records save you from reconstructing the team s history at the end 1 start with the header the dark header displays the sprint name team and product dates and time zone check these before changing anything with suitable permissions you may edit the name and while the sprint is not closed its dates changing dates can affect planning ceremonies and historical interpretation header actions may include generate ai brief generate report and the current sprint status finished and closed are different states closing restricts further changes and may preserve historical snapshots 2 objectives define the expected result the objectives tab explains why the sprint matters beyond a list of tasks 1 review existing sprint objectives 2 select add objective when authorized 3 write a measurable outcome that describes user or business value 4 review the objective when the sprint ends for example customers can view incidents without support is clearer than implement incident screen for some finished sprints authorized users may see enter partial historical review used to complete missing historical information 3 ceremonies keep meetings and outcomes together this tab displays sprint meetings potentially including planning daily scrum review and retrospective ceremonies can be generated when the sprint is created from templates configured in settings the tab shows saved occurrences editing a template later does not necessarily rewrite those already created depending on permissions and sprint status you can review meeting times open a meeting update supported details add suitable meetings or historical records and verify the result in the calendar tip record the outcome of important meetings not only their planned times 4 capacity understand real team availability capacity is not simply headcount multiplied by sprint days smn considers relevant assignments working calendars agile roles and absences the tab can show total person day presence development capacity role specific product owner scrum master capacity member count and a member table with function contribution presence absences and development capacity it also reports when information is missing or ambiguous use manage members or the members screen if your account is authorized to review assignments work patterns and absences remember missing capacity is not zero a closed sprint may show historical snapshots while an open sprint can show projected values 5 indicators explain sprint measurements manual indicators are values recorded for the sprint by authorized users possibly using data from tickets csv computed indicators follow formulas defined in settings indicators team selections and display preferences determine which indicators appear in the cycle detail authorized users can enter manual values and review calculated output in this tab always check the indicator s unit sources and cycle before presenting it a missing value may indicate missing source data rather than a zero result 6 registers preserve the context behind results review sprint risks impediments and dependencies along with relevant decisions actions and highlights where supported use available type filters open records to inspect their status and details and update authorized items while the sprint is not closed the registers module also allows linking related records tip keep resolved impediments in the record they show what the team overcame 7 trends compare several cycles the trends tab displays indicators over multiple sprints where data and permissions allow it check measurement units and indicator definitions before comparing periods changes may be explained by staffing absences scope or other events an empty chart can indicate missing historical data unselected indicators or restricted access tip use a trend to start a discussion not to deliver an automatic judgement about team performance 8 review tell the sprint s story the review tab has distinct spaces for manual review a human authored summary of achievements differences challenges and next steps ai review a place to store or edit an ai related summary the ability to edit it manually does not mean the ai generated it automatically when permitted use the edit control to update content smn can display version author and date closed sprints have editing restrictions and may use closure history suggested structure intended goal observed results differences decisions and next actions 9 prepare closure and reporting before closing or generating a report review all seven tabs 1 are objectives and results clear 2 do ceremonies include meaningful outcomes 3 does capacity reflect member availability 4 are indicators complete and understood 5 are important register records up to date 6 are trends comparable 7 does the review distinguish facts from interpretation the reports module can reuse supported sprint data in compatible word and powerpoint templates 10 troubleshooting missing objectives none may have been recorded yet missing ceremonies check templates and generated occurrences unknown capacity review assignments calendars roles and absences missing indicator check team selection and display preferences missing register record check filters and cycle associations unavailable trend check historical measures and permissions editing blocked check your permissions and whether the sprint is closed your final check can you explain what the team intended what it achieved what capacity was available what events influenced the results and what to improve next if those answers are in the seven tabs your sprint page is a useful team history and planning resource

articles.title: Plan and generate your Scrum sprints
articles.searchText: plan and generate your scrum sprints preparing your next sprint or a whole series smn helps you build a consistent sprint calendar without entering every date by hand the key is to choose the right starting point review the proposal and confirm only when everything looks correct camille s tip check existing sprints before creating any your installation may already contain sample sprints you can explore 1 find your team s sprints 1 open sprints from the navigation 2 check the team shown in the header this is the context for the sprint list 3 explore the all active planned finished and closed status filters 4 use search and sort when the list gets longer select a sprint name to open its details why start here creating another series without checking the current schedule can lead to overlaps or unnecessary sprints if the sprint already exists open it instead of generating a duplicate before generating check your team s sprint cadence where do the dates come from the wizard uses settings team cadence sprint you do not need to re enter each sprint s duration weekdays or times smn reads the selected scrum team s duration in weeks start day and time end day and time and time zone what if you have never configured the cadence smn can automatically create the missing cadence configuration using these default values duration 2 weeks start monday at 09 00 end friday at 18 00 in the second week time zone europe paris before generating a series open the team s cadence settings and check these values defaults make it possible to get started but may not reflect your team s actual working rhythm practical example with the default cadence a wednesday start date is aligned to the following monday the first sprint then ends on the friday of the second week at 18 00 when generating three sprints smn calculates subsequent periods from the same cadence if you have already customized the cadence your saved values take precedence over these defaults always inspect the preview before creating anything if a technical problem prevents the settings from being read or prepared the preview reports an error and generation should not be confirmed 2 open the generation wizard with administrator permissions select generate from the list header the wizard has three stages configure preview and confirm what each field means number of sprints choose how many sprints to create together from 1 to 6 start with 1 while exploring select more when planning several iterations ahead start date enter the start date of the first sprint smn may suggest a date but you should check it before continuing the other dates are calculated using the configured cadence cadence the configured duration weekdays times and time zone determine the proposed periods these settings are not all entered in this wizard if the calculated dates seem wrong review the cadence settings before confirming example to plan three consecutive sprints enter 3 for the number of sprints and choose the first start date smn proposes three periods for review their actual dates depend on your team s cadence select show preview to continue you are still reviewing a proposal no sprint has been confirmed yet 3 review the preview carefully the preview is your opportunity to catch mistakes before they become part of your schedule sprint name smn proposes a name that you can edit up to 160 characters use a consistent naming convention so teammates can find each sprint easily start and end dates check the calculated periods and the displayed time zone pay particular attention to the first and last dates and the transition between periods conflicts this column identifies overlaps with existing or proposed sprints if a conflict appears return to configuration and adjust the proposal ceremony templates active templates may be listed so you know which ceremony templates are available for generation historical ceremonies when working with past dates an additional choice may appear read the warning carefully it concerns historical ceremony handling not sprint duration changed a name or an option select refresh preview the wizard requires an up to date proposal before you can proceed 4 confirm the generation 1 check the number names dates and any blocking conflicts 2 select continue to reach the confirmation stage 3 review the sprint names and any warning displayed 4 select create only when you are satisfied smn returns to the sprint list find the new sprints and open one to inspect its saved details 5 troubleshooting generate is missing creating sprints requires administrator permissions the dates look wrong review the starting date and configured cadence before confirming a conflict is shown check sprints already scheduled for those dates and update your proposal you edited a sprint name select refresh preview before continuing the sprints page is unavailable check that the installation uses scrum mode and you have the necessary access kanban periods follow a different process your final check you should be able to answer which sprints exist what dates do they cover and are they in the right team context once you can answer those questions your sprint calendar is ready remember this guide does not create sprints creation happens only in smn s wizard after you confirm the operation

articles.title: Your team: start with what is already there
articles.searchText: your team start with what is already there before tracking your first sprint take a few minutes to make sure smn reflects your real team there is no need to recreate everything check existing teams first depending on the installation or restore process teams may already be present a fresh native v33 installation with an empty database does not create a team automatically changes here require administrator permissions already have a team make it yours 1 open settings teams 2 find the team you want use search or the active archived filter if needed 3 select the team to open its edit form 4 adapt its name product vision and goal to your work 5 review the scrum or kanban mode it determines which cycles are available and may be locked for an existing team 6 save and confirm the updated details in the list an existing team is usually a better starting point than a duplicate if agile mode cannot be changed review the situation before creating another team no suitable team yet create one 1 in settings teams choose create team in the header 2 enter a recognizable name and select scrum or kanban 3 add the product vision and goal using the information available today 4 confirm then find the new team in the list why these details matter agile mode determines whether smn uses sprints or kanban periods the team also provides the context for members cycles tracking data and reports you can refine details later for now the most important thing is having the right team selected your final check the team name and agile mode are correct product information has been reviewed and there are no duplicates you are ready to move on to team members

articles.title: Tickets / CSV: turn your exports into metrics and history
articles.searchText: tickets csv turn your exports into metrics and history a csv file is more than a list of issues imported into smn at the right moment it becomes a dated snapshot of a sprint or kanban period smn calculates statistics from it supports comparisons over time and can reuse selected snapshots in reports camille s tip think of each import as a measurement over time a snapshot at the start of a sprint and another at the end are much more informative than a single file 1 understand what this module gives you your workflow prepare the csv import a snapshot inspect automatically calculated metrics then compare and reuse the data automatically calculated ticket metrics in browse consultation smn can calculate ticket count number of tickets in the snapshot completed tickets tickets recognized as completed based on their status story point sum sum of usable numeric estimates estimated and unestimated tickets insight into estimation completeness breakdowns ticket counts and story points by type status and id prefix metrics can refer to all tickets or the currently filtered tickets always check the selected scope before quoting a figure using the results in smn indicators the indicators action opens the configured indicators for the selected cycle where authorized users can enter manual indicator values important distinction ticket statistics are calculated automatically in browse but they are not automatically copied into every manual indicator you can use the result as a reference when entering an appropriate manual kpi formula based indicators follow their own definitions example filter by bug and obtain 12 tickets if your indicator catalog includes a manual sprint bug count kpi you can use 12 as a reference while noting the snapshot date and filter scope 2 prepare the expected csv the first line must contain these six required column names older jira header labels are not used id type resume priority status sp what the columns mean id unique issue id such as proj 123 it identifies tickets across snapshots and helps reconstruct jira links when configured type ticket type such as story bug or task resume summary or title priority priority used for filtering status status at the time of export needed for completion counts and comparisons sp story points used for numeric totals and estimation coverage minimal example id type resume priority status sp proj 101 story build the form high done 5 proj 102 bug fix validation medium in progress 3 this example contains 2 tickets 1 completed ticket and 8 story points in total that does not automatically constitute sprint velocity check before importing each required header must occur once the column order may differ and extra columns are allowed ticket ids cannot be empty or duplicated within one file supported separators are commas semicolons and tabs the file must have a csv extension be at most 8 mib and contain no more than 20 000 tickets non numeric story points may produce warnings their original values remain available but they cannot contribute to numeric totals data quality tip use consistent status names in each export completed ticket detection recognizes statuses such as done and termine a custom status is not automatically treated as completed 3 import a dated snapshot 1 open tickets and check the selected team and sprint or kanban period 2 select import csv when authorized 3 verify the cycle shown in the import dialog 4 select your csv file 5 choose the reference date when the snapshot represents the ticket state not necessarily today s import date 6 expand required csv column headers if you need to check the format 7 validate the data fix any reported errors and complete the import why does the reference date matter it tells you when the measurement was taken allowing meaningful comparisons within the same cycle example a csv exported on monday but uploaded on tuesday can keep monday as its reference date if monday is the business date you want to preserve if a snapshot already exists on the selected date smn requires explicit replacement confirmation replacing it changes the current snapshot for that date it does not create another simultaneously browsable snapshot under the same date 4 browse tickets and interpret the metrics in files select the snapshot you want to review you can see its reference date filename import time and ticket count open browse consultation to search filter by type status priority or id prefix sort the results and inspect the calculated metrics check whether metrics describe all records or only filtered ones missing or invalid story points must not be mistaken for zero if configured in settings jira link the base jira address lets smn reconstruct clickable issue urls it does not establish automatic synchronization with jira 5 preserve the history of a sprint or period snapshots are scoped to one team one sprint or kanban period and one reference date this makes it possible to document the work as it evolves a practical approach is to capture cycle start initial scope and estimates mid cycle added changed and completed issues cycle end the final state for review with at least two snapshots on different dates in the same cycle open compare smn can detect added removed completed and reopened tickets story point changes and other recorded changes scrum master tip a higher ticket count does not necessarily mean more progress or more problems interpret the differences alongside the events that happened during the sprint 6 use snapshots in your reports imported snapshots can also serve as data sources in compatible report templates 1 open reports 2 under templates choose a suitable word or powerpoint template 3 select the relevant cycle 4 if the template uses ticket data choose the requested snapshots in the available fields 5 generate or save the document and check the actual ticket tables or comparisons not every report template consumes ticket snapshots the result depends on its tags selected sources and available data importing a csv does not make ticket data appear automatically in every report 7 troubleshooting import csv unavailable check cycle team context and administrative permissions csv rejected verify required headers ids syntax and file limits story point sum missing check non numeric or empty values and any active filters ticket not counted as completed check the status value and recognized conventions compare unavailable add another dated snapshot to the same cycle old snapshot missing check whether it was replaced on the same date or deleted tickets absent from a report verify the template uses ticket data and the correct snapshots were selected your final check can you explain which cycle you measured on what date which metrics smn calculated and which snapshots support your reports if so your csv files have become useful evidence for team tracking rather than isolated exports

articles.title: Working days and hours: configure SMN with confidence
articles.searchText: working days and hours configure smn with confidence this configuration defines work slots and lunch rules for scrum it complements each member s personal work calendar before you change anything look at existing settings and consider which teams and users they affect 1 why configure this section this configuration defines work slots and lunch rules for scrum it complements each member s personal work calendar review it whenever your organization changes or when a feature s results do not match your expectations 2 open the right screen 1 open settings 2 find working days and hours in the settings catalog 3 select its entry when available the related screen is here 4 check your access rights the selected team and the current values 3 follow the configuration workflow 1 open settings then working days in a scrum context 2 under slots verify the team and proposed work windows 3 adjust working days and hours to match team practice 4 under lunch break review the configured lunch rule 5 save and check the calendar and individual schedules 4 understand the fields and their effects team slots provide a shared frame an individual s schedule may differ and should be recorded in their member profile what changes after save the resulting configuration is used by the related smn module existing business records or already generated documents are not necessarily changed retroactively 5 practical guidance do not model a one off absence as a permanent working day change use absences for exceptions if the option is unavailable check your permissions the installation mode and whether the settings catalog marks it as planned or only partially available your final check can you explain what was changed why what it affects and how to verify it in the relevant screen if yes the setup is meaningful and ready for daily use
